headline: The Windows XP hill is a real place. And the photo wasn't edited.
slides: Photographer Charles O'Rear was driving through Sonoma County to see his girlfriend.
He pulled over on the side of the road and shot the hill on film, with a Mamiya RZ67.
Vineyards there had been ripped out after a pest infestation, so it was just grass after winter rain.
Microsoft bought the rights and renamed it Bliss.
As the Windows XP wallpaper, it's thought to be the most viewed photograph in history.
The hill has been replanted with vines. It doesn't look like that any more.
sources: Sources: Wikipedia (Bliss), PCWorld, Digital Camera World, New York Daily News (2014)
